Title: Business Development Representative
Description:
#### **Business Development Representative (BDR)**

Department: Sales

Reports to: Sales Manager

Type: Full Time

Work Type: Onsite

Salary Range: $50,000 – $65,000 per year plus Commissions

#### **About Us:**

Winsor Consulting Group is a leading Managed Service Provider (MSP) committed to delivering exceptional IT and infrastructure solutions to our clients. Our expertise includes Managed Services, Professional Services, Security & Compliance, Data Center and Colocation, and Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS).

We are seeking a motivated and results-driven Business Development Representative (BDR) to expand our market presence, develop new business relationships, and generate qualified sales opportunities across Winsor's technology portfolio.

#### **Job Description:**

The Business Development Representative will focus on identifying prospective clients, initiating business relationships, scheduling qualified first-time appointments, and building a consistent sales pipeline.

The ideal candidate is a proactive, self-motivated individual who enjoys prospecting, building relationships, and uncovering business opportunities. This individual should be comfortable conducting initial discovery conversations, understanding client challenges, and identifying potential technology solutions.

While primarily focused on pipeline development, the BDR may also independently manage and close qualified opportunities. The BDR will collaborate with Sales Representatives, Sales Engineering, Marketing, and Service Operations to advance opportunities and support revenue growth.

This position offers opportunities to develop technical sales knowledge, strengthen consultative selling skills, and grow within Winsor's Sales organization.

#### **Job Duties:**

#### **Business Development Representative**

* Identify, research, prospect, and develop new business opportunities within assigned markets and territories.
* Generate new opportunities through outbound calling, email campaigns, LinkedIn outreach, networking, referrals, and other business development activities.
* Schedule and conduct qualified firsttime appointments (FTAs) with prospective clients.
* Develop and maintain a consistent pipeline of new business opportunities across Winsor's Managed Services, Professional Services, Data Center, Colocation, IaaS, and Security & Compliance offerings.
* Lead initial business discovery conversations to understand client challenges, technology needs, business objectives, and potential opportunities.
* Qualify prospective opportunities by identifying business needs, decisionmakers, timelines, and potential service requirements.
* Develop an understanding of Winsor's service offerings and identify opportunities where multiple solutions may benefit a prospective client.
* Build and maintain relationships with business owners, executives, IT leaders, and other key decisionmakers.
* Manage and advance assigned sales opportunities through the sales cycle, including independently closing opportunities when appropriate.
* Collaborate with Sales Representatives, Sales Engineering, and technical teams when additional expertise is needed to develop solutions or advance opportunities.
* Maintain accurate and uptodate prospecting activities, client interactions, sales opportunities, and pipeline information in CRM systems such as HubSpot and ConnectWise Manage.
* Follow up consistently with prospective clients to maintain engagement and advance opportunities.
* Develop relationships with referral partners, technology vendors, and other organizations capable of generating new business opportunities.
* Participate in networking events, industry events, business meetings, and other activities that support new business development.
* Work with Marketing and Sales leadership to identify target markets, develop outreach strategies, and improve leadgeneration efforts.
* Monitor prospecting activity, firsttime appointments, qualified opportunities, and pipeline development against established goals.
* Meet or exceed assigned sales activity, pipeline development, revenue, and performance expectations.

#### **Preferred Skills:**

* Strong prospecting, relationshipbuilding, and business development skills.
* Comfortable initiating conversations with new prospects through phone, email, networking, and other outreach methods.
* Ability to lead business conversations, ask effective discovery questions, and identify potential client needs.
* Strong communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills.
* Ability to develop and maintain relationships with business owners, executives, and technology decisionmakers.
* Interest in technology and willingness to learn Managed Services, Professional Services, Data Center, Colocation, Cloud, and infrastructure solutions.
* Ability to recognize business challenges and work with technical resources to identify appropriate solutions.
* Strong organizational, followup, and timemanagement skills.
* Experience with CRM systems such as HubSpot, ConnectWise Manage, Salesforce, or similar platforms.
* Selfmotivated, persistent, accountable, and comfortable working toward measurable performance goals.
* Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with Sales, Marketing, Sales Engineering, and technical teams.
* Strong problemsolving skills and willingness to continuously develop sales and technical knowledge.

#### **Experience:**

* 1+ years of experience in business development, B2B sales, lead generation, account development, or a related clientfacing role preferred.
* Experience with outbound prospecting, relationship development, or appointment setting is preferred.
* Experience working within an IT services provider, Managed Service Provider (MSP), technology company, telecommunications provider, cloud provider, or Data Center organization is beneficial but not required.
* Experience generating qualified sales opportunities and managing sales pipeline activity is preferred.
* Demonstrated ability to meet activity goals, develop relationships, and consistently follow through on business opportunities.
* Candidates with strong sales aptitude, communication skills, and a willingness to learn will be considered even without direct technology sales experience.

#### **Preferred Certifications:**

* Relevant sales training or certifications such as Sandler, MEDDICC, Challenger, or equivalent are preferred but not required.
* Vendor or technology certifications related to Managed Services, Cloud, Infrastructure, Data Center, or Microsoft technologies are beneficial but not required.

#### **Education:**

* High school diploma or equivalent required. A Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Communications, Information Technology, or a related field is preferred but not required. Relevant work experience, sales aptitude, and demonstrated performance will be strongly considered in place of formal education.

#### **Performance Expectations**

Success in this position will be measured primarily through consistent business development activity and the ability to create qualified sales opportunities.

#### **Key performance measurements will include:**

* Outbound prospecting and business development activity.
* Qualified firsttime appointments (FTAs).
* New prospective client relationships established.
* Qualified sales opportunities and pipeline generated.
* Consistent followup and opportunity progression.
* CRM accuracy and pipeline management.
* Closed revenue and achievement of assigned sales goals.

The successful candidate will be expected to demonstrate consistent prospecting activity, pipeline development, and the generation of qualified sales opportunities for Winsor's Sales Representatives. While the primary focus is creating new business opportunities, the BDR will also have opportunities to independently manage and close sales as their knowledge and experience develop.

#### **Commission Structure:**

Compensation is comprised of base salary plus performance-based commission. Winsor's BDR commission structure rewards the generation of qualified new business opportunities that result in closed sales, with commission calculations varying by solution type.

#### **BDR-Generated Opportunities**

When a BDR identifies and qualifies a new business opportunity that is subsequently closed by a Sales Representative, the BDR earns a sourcing commission based on the following rates. The sourcing commission is allocated from the existing Outside Sales commission, with the remaining commission paid to the closing Sales Representative.

#### **Managed Services and Colocation**

Earn up to 15% of the first month's gross margin on qualifying agreements, based on the agreement term:

* 36month agreement: 15%
* 24month agreement: 10%
* 12month agreement: 5%

Commissions are paid over seven months in accordance with the applicable commission agreement

#### **Staff Augmentation**

Earn 0.5% of qualifying labor fees on Staff Augmentation engagements, paid based on applicable client payments and service delivery.

#### **Professional Services Projects**

Earn 1% of qualifying Professional Services labor revenue, paid as client payments are received.

#### **Hardware and One-Time Software**

Earn 1.5% of gross margin on qualifying hardware and one-time software sales.

#### **SaaS Agreements**

Earn up to 15% of the first month's gross margin on qualifying agreements, based on the agreement term:

* 36month agreement: 15%
* 24month agreement: 10%
* 12month agreement: 5%

#### **Referrals and Carrier Opportunities**

Earn 1.5% of qualifying net commissions received by Winsor from referral and carrier opportunities.

#### **Partner Resale Opportunities**

Earn 1.5% of gross margin on qualifying partner resale opportunities.

#### **BDR-Closed Opportunities**

When a BDR independently manages and closes an assigned sales opportunity, they are eligible to earn the full applicable commission as defined in Winsor's Outside Sales Commission Agreement.

Winsor Consulting Group is a trusted Managed Services Provider delivering comprehensive IT solutions to businesses across Iowa, Illinois, Arizona, and beyond. We provide security focused fully managed IT services, professional services for project-based initiatives, data center services, and compliance solutions that allow organizations to focus on their business while we manage their technology.

Title: SVP, IT Operations
Description:
**SUMMARY**

The Senior Vice President, IT Operations is accountable for the stability, performance, resilience, secure operation and continuous improvement of the technology environment that supports BGIS operations and the business-critical solutions we deliver to our clients. Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, this executive leads four operational domains: Application Support, Infrastructure (including Service Desk and End User Support), Financial Application Support, and the Legacy Software Development Platform (operational enhancements). The individual sets the operational strategy and service model for these domains, directs a team of directors, managers and technical professionals across onshore and offshore teams, and partners with business unit leaders, client-facing teams and vendors to ensure that services meet or exceed contractual SLAs and client expectations. The individual drives a culture of operational excellence and continuous improvement, using automation, standardization, data-driven KPI management and modern IT service management practices to increase reliability, reduce cost, and improve the client and end-user experience. The role is a member of the IT leadership team and reports regularly to senior and executive management on operational performance, risk and investment priorities.

**KEY DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES**

Leadership

Directs the IT Operations organization through a team of directors and managers, spanning onshore, offshore and third-party resources across all four domains.

Demonstrates strong, competent leadership for team members to guide them in reaching their full potential and meeting their objectives, which supports achievement of our corporate goals. Specifically, these responsibilities include but not limited to:

* Full involvement with recruiting talent.
* Provides mentoring, coaching and guidance to all team members.
* Objectively recommends compensation adjustments.
* Manages all aspects of performance.
* Builds leadership bench strength and succession plans across all four IT Operations domains.
* Develops the technical capabilities of the organization, including reskilling and upskilling staff for cloud, automation and AI-enabled operations.
* Defines the workforce and sourcing strategy, determining the right balance of in-house, offshore and managed service resources.
Fosters an environment of teamwork, accountability, innovation and client service to meet business objectives.  

IT Operations Strategy & Service Excellence

* Defines and executes the multi-year IT Operations strategy and roadmap, aligned with BGIS business objectives, client commitments and the broader IT strategy.
* Partners with the Chief Technology Officer and Architecture to shape the enterprise technology roadmap and standards, and leads the operational integration of acquired businesses and new technology platforms.
* Holds overall accountability for the availability, performance and resiliency of business-critical solutions that support our clients, ensuring contractual SLAs and KPIs are consistently met or exceeded.
* Establishes a unified operating model, service catalogue and support structure (L1-L3) across Application Support, Infrastructure, Financial Application Support and the Legacy Software Development Platform.
* Establishes demand intake, prioritization and resource capacity planning across all four domains, balancing day-to-day operations, operational projects, CISO-requested security work and client commitments, and ensures operational projects are delivered on time, on budget and with minimal service disruption.
* Establishes governance for ITSM processes, including incident, major incident, problem, change, release, configuration and request management, and ensures timely root-cause analysis and corrective action.
* Ensures 24x7 operational coverage for business-critical services, including monitoring and event management, and on-call and after-hours support.
* Serves as the executive escalation point for critical client-impacting incidents; directs response, client communication and post-incident reviews.
* Builds relationships with senior business unit leaders and client-facing teams to understand business direction, anticipate operational needs and manage expectations.
* Provides service performance insights to account and client-facing teams to inform client governance discussions and shape the support model, and ensures IT services comply with client contractual, audit and data protection requirements.
* Establishes and enforces IT Operations policies, standards and procedures, and ensures adherence to enterprise IT standards (i.e. Security, IT Governance, Service Management, Architecture).
* Manages operational risks through mitigation strategies, and plans or implements contingencies where necessary.
Provides regular reporting to senior and executive management on SLA and KPI performance, operational risk, capacity and investment priorities.  

Application Support

* Directs the support, maintenance and operational health of the enterprise and client-facing application portfolio, including integrations, middleware and SaaS platforms.
* Ensures applications that support client service delivery are monitored, supported and maintained to meet defined service levels and business continuity requirements.
* Partners with Business Technology, product and development teams to ensure smooth transition of new solutions into production support, including defining operational acceptance criteria early in the delivery lifecycle.
* Sets the strategy for application lifecycle management, including patching, upgrades, license compliance, and the rationalization and decommissioning of redundant applications.
Oversees database administration and data operations, including performance, backup and restore, and data retention, in line with BGIS and client requirements.  

Infrastructure & End User Support

* Leads the strategy, engineering and operation of the infrastructure environment, including data centre and cloud platforms, servers, storage, networks and telephony.
* Directs the Service Desk and End User Support functions, including end-user computing, mobile devices, collaboration tools and field support, ensuring a consistent, high-quality experience for employees and client-facing staff.
* Ensures infrastructure capacity, performance and resiliency meet current and future business and client requirements.
* Owns IT disaster recovery and partners with the Business Continuity Planning (BCP) team to ensure IT systems meet BCP objectives; ensures DR plans are documented and tested regularly.
* Establishes IT asset and configuration management practices, including hardware and software asset lifecycle and an accurate configuration management database (CMDB).
Advances infrastructure modernization, including cloud adoption, observability, AIOps and infrastructure automation.  

Financial Application Support

* Directs the operation, support and operational enhancement of the financial application landscape (e.g. ERP, general ledger, accounts payable/receivable, billing, procurement and related integrations).
* Partners with Finance leadership to ensure financial systems reliably support month-end, quarter-end and year-end close, client billing and financial reporting cycles.
* Ensures appropriate IT general controls, segregation of duties and audit readiness in support of internal controls over financial reporting and internal and external audit requirements.
Establishes governance with Finance stakeholders for prioritizing financial system changes, enhancements and upgrades.  

Legacy Software Development Platform (Operational Enhancements)

* Leads the team responsible for sustaining and enhancing legacy and custom-developed software platforms that continue to support business-critical operations and client solutions.
* Establishes the intake and prioritization framework for operational enhancements, defect fixes and minor changes, balancing business value, risk and capacity.
* Ensures sound software change management practices, including source control, release and deployment management, testing, quality assurance and release sign-off.
Reduces technical debt and operational risk of legacy platforms, and partners with Architecture and Business Technology to define modernization, migration or retirement roadmaps.  

Security & Compliance Support

* Partners with the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), delivering the technology work required for security projects and programs as they are raised.
* Ensures operational security practices are consistently executed across IT Operations in accordance with CISO-defined policies, including access management, vulnerability and patch management, backup and secure configuration.
* Supports the CISO during security incidents by providing technical response, recovery and remediation resources.
Supports compliance, certification and client audit activities by providing operational evidence and remediating identified gaps.  

Continuous Improvement

* Champions a culture of continuous improvement, using operational data, trend analysis and client feedback to identify and remove recurring issues and inefficiencies.
* Drives automation, self-service, standardization and AI-enabled tooling to improve service quality, speed of resolution and cost-effectiveness.
* Ensures knowledge management, runbooks and documentation practices are maintained across all IT Operations domains to enable shift-left resolution, self-service and reduced reliance on key individuals.
* Establishes meaningful, business-focused KPIs and dashboards for each domain and uses them to set improvement targets and measure progress.
* Introduces and matures industry best practices (e.g. ITIL, Lean, SRE and DevOps principles) across IT Operations.
* Applies BGIS AI policies and establishes operating guidelines for the responsible use of AI and automation within IT Operations.
Evaluates emerging technologies and recommends investments that improve reliability, reduce risk and deliver value to our clients.  

Financial & Vendor Management

* Develops and manages the IT Operations operating and capital budgets; identifies opportunities for cost optimization while protecting service quality.
* Applies cloud financial management (FinOps) practices to monitor, allocate and optimize cloud consumption costs.
* Manages strategic vendor, managed service provider and outsourcing relationships, including contract negotiation, performance management and SLA governance.
* Ensures managed service providers, offshore and third-party resources meet BGIS and client security, privacy and contractual obligations, in partnership with the CISO and Procurement.
* Supports proposal and client transition teams by defining operational support models and service commitments, and ensures client data, access and integrations are transitioned or decommissioned in line with contractual obligations when client contracts end.
Other duties as assigned.  

**Knowledge & Skills**

* Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Business or equivalent; Master's Degree or MBA is an asset.
* Minimum 15 years of progressive IT experience, including at least 8 years in senior leadership roles within IT Operations, infrastructure and application support.
* Proven experience leading large, multi-disciplinary teams through multiple layers of management, including onshore, offshore and third-party resources.
* Demonstrated track record of supporting business-critical, client-facing solutions in a service delivery or outsourced services environment with contractual SLAs.
* Strong working knowledge of enterprise infrastructure (cloud, data centre, network, end-user computing), service desk operations, application support, and IT service management (ITIL) practices.
* Experience supporting financial/ERP systems and IT general controls in an audited environment.
* Working knowledge of security and privacy frameworks and regulations (e.g. ISO 27001, SOC 2, NIST, PIPEDA) as they apply to IT operations.
* Experience sustaining and modernizing legacy and custom-developed software platforms, including software change and release management.
* Proven ability to drive continuous improvement, automation and operational transformation with measurable results.
* Exceptionally skilled business and financial management ability, including management of operating and capital budgets.
* Exceptionally skilled at influencing, negotiating and building relationships with senior management and executives.
* Highly skilled at managing vendor performance and complex service contracts.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to articulate complex technical ideas in easy to understand business terms.
* Calm, decisive leadership under pressure, with the ability to direct response to major incidents.
Experience in the Real Estate or Facilities Management domain is desirable.  

**Licenses and/or Professional Accreditation**

* ITIL certification is required (Expert or Managing Professional preferred).
PMP, Lean Six Sigma, or cloud platform certifications are an asset.

GLOBAL TECHNICAL SERVICES LEADER
  
  
**Job Description**
**ACT Entertainment**
DEPARTMENT: Sales FLSA: Exempt (Salaried)
  
  
**REPORTS TO: Chief Revenue Officer LOCATION : Cincinnati, OH (US) or London (UK)**
**REPORTS TO:**
Chief Revenue Officer
**LOCATION**
: Cin
  
  
For more than 40 years, ACT Entertainment has been at the forefront of the entertainment technology industry. Our innovation has helped shape the future of how the world experiences music, audio, and live sound, and we are just getting started.
  
  
**Position Summary:**
ACT Entertainment is hiring a Global Tech Services Leader to take single-point ownership of service delivery worldwide. Today, hardware service, software support, and service coordination across Lighting, Video, and Interconnects are coordinated informally. This leader will unify those three departments under shared standards, build out the functions that are underdeveloped, and carry P&L responsibility. You will be the face of Tech Services to our supplier partners and the owner of global service quality, consistency, and growth.
  
  
**Duties & Responsibilities:**
****Leadership and Organization****

* Own end-to-end accountability for Hardware Service, Software Support, and Service Coordinators globally.
* Directly manage existing hardware and software service leads, aligning them to shared standards, KPIs, and tooling.
* Directly own Interconnects Hardware Service until a dedicated lead is needed, then transition day-to-day ownership while retaining oversight.
* Build a management layer that brings each manager's workload to a sustainable level and supports succession and scalability.
* Represent Tech Services in leadership planning, budget, and headcount decisions.
* Oversee cross-department interactions and processes- Purchasing, Sales, Accounting, Operations, Traffic, Logistics, among others. Codify processes into SOPs and update, improve, or develop new ones as needed.

****Service Standards and Operations****

* Establish global service-level standards, escalation paths, and a reporting cadence across all departments and product categories.
* Align North America and UK Lighting, and North America and International Video, on common processes, communication, and customer satisfaction measures.
* Rationalize the current ticketing systems to reduce cost and close communication gaps for global customers.

****Service Coordination****

* Stand up and lead the service coordinator’s function, defining its structure, staffing, and how it supports the other departments globally, including international coverage.

**Supplier Partners**

* Act as the technical communication and relationship conduit for supplier partners.
* Communicate a clear strategic direction and a credible technical agenda to keep partners confident and invested in ACT.

****Financial Ownership****

* Hold P&L responsibility for service revenue across hardware service and software support.
* Work with Finance and Sales to build and own a departmental budget and forecast, operating within the budget defined during onboarding.
* Review service structure, costing, warranty scope, and pricing, and bring visibility to service labor and parts costs across all regions.
* Lead regular P&L reviews with Finance and leadership on revenue, cost of service, and margin trends.

**Other Responsibilities**

* Perform other related duties as assigned.

**Supervisory Responsibilities:**

* Leads the existing hardware and software service leaders in North America, the UK, and internationally; builds out Service Coordinators .
* P&L responsibility for annual service revenue

**Qualifications:**

* High school diploma or GED required; associate’s degree, technical degree or bachelor’s degree preferred.
* Proven leadership of a multi-discipline, multi-region technical services organization, comparable to a Director or VP of Technical Services.
* Previous hands-on technical credibility in hardware and software service for professional lighting, video, or interconnect products.
* Demonstrated P&L ownership, including budgeting, cost of service, pricing, and margin management.
* Experience managing managers and leading distributed teams across North America and Europe.
* Strong communication skills and ability to represent technical direction to manufacturers and supplier partners.
* Previous experience consolidating service tools, such as ticketing systems, and standardizing processes across regions preferred.
* Experience in entertainment technology, live events, or distribution businesses preferred.
* Ability to travel up to 40%, both domestic and international travel.

**Company Values:**

* Deliver Legendary Service: It’s all about the experience. With every experience, do the little things, as well as the big things, that surprise people. Make every interaction stand out for its helpfulness. Create the “WOW” factor that turns customers into raving fans. This includes both internal and external customers.
* Do the Right Thing, Always: Demonstrate an unwavering commitment to doing the right thing in every action you take and in every decision you make, especially when no one’s looking . Always tell the truth, no matter the consequences. If you make a mistake, own up to it, apologize, and make it right.
* Practice Blameless Problem-Solving: Demonstrate a relentless solution focus, rather than pointing fingers or dwelling on problems. Identify lessons learned and use those lessons to improve ourselves and our processes so we don’t make the same mistake twice. Get smarter with every mistake. Learn from every experience.
* Contribute to Profit: We’re in business to deliver value for our customers while making money. We all play a role in building revenue that exceeds our expenses. Look for ways to increase our sales, develop new customers, and control our expenses.
* Honor Commitments: Do what you say you’re going to do, when you say you’re going to do it. This includes being on time for all phone calls, appointments, and meetings. If a commitment can’t be fulfilled, notify others early and agree on a new deliverable to be honored.
* Embrace Change and Growth: What got us here is not the same as what will get us to the next level. Get outside your comfort zone, rather than stubbornly hanging on to old ways of doing things. Be excited by the possibilities that change, and growth bring. Be flexible.
* Be Positive: You have the power to choose your attitude. Choose to be joyful, optimistic, and enthusiastic. See the good in others. Your attitude is contagious. Spread optimism and positive energy.
* Keep Things Fun: While our passion for excellence is real, remember that the world has bigger problems than the daily challenges that make up our work. Stuff happens. Keep perspective. Don’t take things personally or take yourself too seriously. Laugh every day.

**Physical Demands:**

* Occasionally required to stand.
* Occasionally required to walk.
* Continually required to sit for long periods.
* Continually required to utilize hand and finger dexterity.
* The employee must lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.
* Specific vision abilities required by this job include: close vision; distance vision; color vision; peripheral vision; depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

**JOB DESCRIPTION**

**TITLE:** Executive Director

**POSITION SUMMARY:**

Provide creative, visionary leadership and direction for CAMREC programs and staff. First-year priorities are financial stability through increased use, appropriate pricing and fundraising; revitalizing summer camp and supporting volunteer-led retreats; and improving website, social media, email and newsletter communications. Work with the Board, staff and volunteers to advance CAMREC’s mission.

The Executive Director reports to the CAMREC Board. The Board sets policy and approves budgets; the Executive Director implements Board decisions and manages operations within approved budgets, Personnel Policies and written delegations. Coordinate with committees and respect designated staff reporting arrangements, including conflict-of-interest safeguards.

**DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:1. Program**

a. Oversee program implementation.

b. Work year-round with the Program Committee to plan, recruit for, prepare and evaluate summer youth camp. Supervise the seasonal Summer Program Director during the six-week appointment.

c. Provide vision for programming that meets constituent needs; recruit and support volunteers to organize WMF retreats using clear schedules, budgets, registration, promotion and hosting arrangements.

d. Oversee quality of the programs.

e. Evaluate programs and ensure recommended improvements occur.

f. Ensure appropriate medical arrangements, staff screening, orientation, documentation and safety preparations are completed before programs begin.

**2. Staff**

a. Recruit, hire, orient, supervise, support and evaluate staff within approved budgets, CAMREC Personnel Policies and Board-delegated authority. Follow policy and reserved Board authority for dismissals. Keep the Board informed and include Board representatives in year-round interviews and selection.

b. Evaluate year-round staff based on job description and goals of each position.

c. Maintain current job descriptions, personnel procedures, confidential records and regular performance feedback. Recommend policy and compensation changes for Board approval.

d. Provide opportunities for staff development and spiritual and personal growth.

e. Attend conferences and other educational opportunities that provide training and enhance job performance and satisfaction. Encourage year round staff to seek similar opportunities.

f. Recruit and coordinate volunteers and Voluntary Service worker(s) with designated supervisors and clear accountability for essential functions.

g. Work to foster a culture of collaboration, support, empowerment, creativity, and integrity.

**3. Business Administration**

a. Monitor expenditures and income, operating within the constraints of the approved budget unless approval is otherwise given by the Board.

b. Administer financial operations in consultation with the Treasurer; i.e. bookkeeping of rentals, program fees, donations, etc.

c. Develop specific policies, practices and procedures for camp operations and programs focusing first on safety and professionalism.

d. Maintain adequate insurance: general liability, property, medical, vehicle, accident, etc.

e. Maintain all federal, state, and local standards and file reports as required.

f. Understand tax exempt status of Camrec as it relates to rental and programming options.

g. Ensure timely rental responses and backup coverage. Manage the booking calendar, approved rates, agreements, deposits, confirmations, billing and collections.

h. Track inquiry sources, conversion to bookings, unused dates and guest feedback; improve rental procedures and develop new and repeat business.

i. Design and implement programs that address the capital and operational expenses of Camp Camrec.

j. Collect and preserve items of historical value such as photos, reports, minutes, etc.

**4. Public Relations, Marketing, and Fundraising**

a. Represent camp at WMF and local churches and be available to give programs and presentations.

b. Work with staff, board members, and volunteers in promotion and publicity.

c. Prepare and distribute promotional materials, brochures, exhibits, and newsletters.

d. Maintain accurate, timely website content, social media, email communications, registration and payment information.

e. Respond to concerns, compliments and inquiries relating to all aspects of camp.

f. Develop marketing strategies.

g. Seek ways to share ownership of the Mission of Camp Camrec with board, staff, volunteers, and constituents.

h. Lead donor cultivation, appeals and suitable grant applications with the Board. Maintain gift and grant records and required reports; support endowment development while respecting restrictions and Board authority.

**5. Board Activities**

a. Submit agenda items to the Board Chair for meetings.

b. Provide concise reports of camp activities for Board meetings.

c. Prepare concise year-end reports. Annually present goals to the Board.

d. Prepare the recommendation for the annual budget in concert with the Treasurer and present this draft to the Board for approval in advance of the WMF Annual Meeting.

e. Be a channel of communication with the Board for the staff.

f. Give vision to and implement the long term strategic plan.

**6. General**

a. Coordinate facilities and land stewardship with the Facilities Manager, Land Steward and Facilities & Land Committee. Ensure priorities, essential coverage, capital planning and wildfire resilience without assuming all hands-on duties personally.

b. Coordinate housekeeping and hospitality through assigned staff. When a Guest Services Manager is appointed, assign that role the lead for guest cleaning arrangements and departure inspections; the Facilities Manager leads repairs, maintenance supplies, waste disposal and kitchen-linen washing. Designate backup coverage whenever a role is vacant or unavailable.

c. Maintain emergency plans, safeguarding procedures, incident follow-up, secure system access and operational continuity.

d. Monitor and purchase office supplies.

e. Manage, and upgrade as needed, technology used at camp, including phone, internet, website and wifi.

**DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

1. Commitment to CAMREC’s mission and support for Mennonite/Anabaptist values, including peace, hospitality, community and care for creation.

2. Passionate about furthering the Mission of Camp Camrec.

3. Relevant educational background and/or experience working/volunteering at a camp/retreat center. Relevant camp leadership experience is preferred.

4. Desire to build relationships with church and community leaders.

5. Possess strong leadership and relational skills, knowledge of camp programs, good communication and speaking skills, computer skills, administrative skills, and energy.

6. Flexible to the ebb and flow of a camp operation, appreciation for both large groups of people and solitude.

**HOW TO APPLY:**

Email info@camrec.org with the subject “Executive Director Application”, including:

* Cover letter describing your interest, relevant experience, support for CAMREC’s mission, earliest start date, relocation timing and willingness to live on site, and desired pay (recognizing that housing, internet, and utilities are provided).
* Résumé and three references or

**Applications will be accepted until the position is filled.**

Benefits:

* Flexible schedule
* Paid time off
* Retirement plan

The Supplier Fulfilment Leader manages delivery, demand translation, and production planning for an assigned part family, balancing efficient inventory management for work-in-process (WIP) against supplier capacity constraints. Working in close collaboration with the internal make shops and Site Materials teams, the role facilitates supplier problem solving for the assigned parts and owns execution of complex, multi-year, multi-site source changes that support improved connected flow within the part family.  
Delivery-first role for a seasoned professional with a manufacturing production planning background who understands how master schedules, MRP, and shop-floor sequencing translate into supplier demand, and what a late or short shipment costs the line. The role leads through influence, partnering with Sourcing, Production Planning, Quality, Engineering, and Finance.

**Job Description**
===================

**Key Responsibilities**
========================

* **Define and improve sourcing strategy.** Manage sourcing strategies at the part family and supplier level, including execution of connected flow in line with a decentralized organization structure.
* **Translate demand into level supplier schedules.** Absorb the total demand profile from all end items requiring the supplier's processes and convert it into a level production schedule within suppliers.
* **Own supplier delivery performance.** Drive on-time, delivery (OTD) for assigned suppliers and parts; set targets, track results, and hold suppliers accountable to commitments.
* **Manage external WIP and commitments.** Manage supplier WIP, commits, and recommits; integrate loop design, input plan, delivery, return store levels, supplier WIP, and supplier performance.
* **Lead shortage recovery.** Run shortage reviews, expedite and escalate critical items, and execute structured recovery plans that protect line-down and customer-delivery risk.
* **Analyze capability and capacity.** Assess supplier capability and total capacity for the defined production areas; identify at-risk suppliers and parts early and develop contingencies such as alternate sources, buffer stock, and re-sequencing.
* **Align with S&OP and Site Materials.** In partnership with Site Materials Leaders, collaborate with external S&OP, forecasting, and product line teams to surface and resolve constraints; help define and apply elements of the production system and set the pace for upstream supply chain.
* **Lead supplier communication.** Lead communication and response to all assigned suppliers; use on-site presence at the Houston-area supplier to drive problem solving alongside supplier production, planning, and quality teams.
* **Report and improve.** Manage team metrics and reporting to support team and part family bowler metrics; apply Lean and continuous-improvement tools to eliminate recurring root causes of late delivery.
* **Influence and develop others.** Serve as a best-practice resource and mentor to less experienced colleagues; lead projects with large-scale business impact and build consensus on sensitive or complex topics.

**Required Qualifications**
===========================

* Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university. Minimum of 5 years of sourcing and sourcing management experience, with demonstrated production planning, master scheduling, or materials planning background in a manufacturing environment.

**Preferred Qualifications**
============================

* Experience in Aerospace, defense, or other high-reliability, long-lead-time manufacturing; experience with forgings, castings, or rotating parts supply bases.
* APICS/ASCM certification (CPIM, CSCP) or equivalent.
* Lean training or certification.
* Experience with supplier development, ramp-up, and multi-site source transitions.
* Proven track record of improving supplier delivery performance and resolving material shortages in a complex, high-mix or regulated manufacturing environment.
* Working knowledge of MRP/ERP systems and planning concepts: lead time, safety stock, BOM structure, planning parameters, and constraint-based scheduling.
* Strong data analysis skills (Excel, BI tools) to support recommendations and decisions.
* Excellent communication, negotiation, and escalation skills; able to influence suppliers and senior stakeholders and to explain difficult or sensitive information.
* Sound judgment and the ability to make decisions under pressure with moderate autonomy within broad guidelines and policies.

**Desired Characteristics**
===========================

* **Humble:** respectful, receptive, agile, eager to learn.
* **Transparent:** shares critical information, speaks with candor, contributes constructively.
* **Focused:** quick learner, strategically prioritizes work, committed.
* **Leadership ability:** strong communicator, decision-maker, collaborative.
* **Problem solver:** analytical-minded, challenges existing processes, critical thinker.

**Core Competencies**
=====================

* **Delivery mindset:** Relentless focus on commitments, with a bias for action and clear ownership.
* **Manufacturing acumen:** Understands how supply shortfalls affect shop-floor flow, cost, and customer commitments.
* **Influence and collaboration:** Builds trust and aligns suppliers and internal partners around shared outcomes.
* **Problem solving:** Gets to root cause quickly and implements durable corrective actions.
* **Integrity and compliance:** Upholds company values, ethics, and regulatory requirements.

**Success Measures**
====================

* Supplier OTD and schedule adherence for assigned scope.
* Reduction in past-due value, critical shortages, and line-down events.
* Accuracy and stability of supplier promise dates versus plan.
* Speed and quality of recovery plans and escalation closure.
* Improvement in supplier scorecard ratings and recurring root causes eliminated.

* Translate emerging scientific trends and competitive intelligence into actionable platform investments and capability-building initiatives

* Foster an inclusive, high-performance team culture that leverages diverse scientific backgrounds and cross-site perspectives to achieve platform objectives

* Provide strategic direction to Senior Scientists overseeing the full lifecycle management of regulated cellular immunology assays — from method development and qualification through validation, execution, and lifecycle maintenance — ensuring scientific integrity and regulatory defensibility

  

* Serve as the senior scientific authority for cellular immunology-related quality events, including deviations, corrective and preventive actions, and change controls, providing strategic direction on investigation and resolution

  

* Ensure platform-wide compliance with good practice standards, laboratory testing regulations, and Sanofi quality systems, including laboratory information management system governance, reagent qualification, and documentation standards

  

* Lead platform readiness for regulatory inspections and audits, serving as the senior subject matter expert for precision cellular immunology methodologies in interactions with regulatory authorities

  
  
Translational Research Integration & Scientific Harmonization
  
  

* Establish scientific bridges between translational and clinical work streams, enabling the efficient translation of novel biomarkers and immunological endpoints — including those derived from single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics — from research into validated clinical assays

  

* Drive the development of integrated data strategies that leverage both clinical and translational datasets to generate mechanistic insights supporting vaccine candidate advancement

  

* Collaborate with Global Regulatory Affairs, Clinical Development, and Translational Medicine to define immunological endpoints and biomarker strategies for early- and late-phase vaccine programs

  
  
Technology Innovation & Digital Transformation
  
  

* Set the strategic direction for the platform's technology and automation roadmap, providing oversight to the staff who lead the hands-on evaluation, implementation, and optimization of automated liquid-handling systems, robotic platforms, and emerging immunological technologies

  

* Champion the development and implementation of high-dimensional data pipelines to manage complex spectral flow cytometry, single-cell RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomics datasets and enable AI/ML-driven immunological analysis

Enterprise Stakeholder Management & External Representation

Overview:

Shamal Holding is a diversified investment firm that cultivates the extraordinary. Born in Dubai, we curate a unique portfolio of extraordinary investments, experiences and assets to generate meaningful outcomes. The investments we make are strategically chosen and thoughtfully nurtured, mirroring Dubai’s ambition, spirit and energy. As a global investor, asset owner and developer we utilise our resources, know-how and connections, to deliver long-term value, wherever we operate.

As Shamal Holding continues to grow, we’re in search of a **Destination Director – Communities & Facilities Management**. In this role, you will role be responsible to deliver Facilities Management Services to Leasehold and Business Unit assets as a consistently premium, hospitality-led destination by translating Shamal's vision into measurable outcomes across resident and guest experience, service performance, asset presentation, stakeholder confidence, commercial discipline and long-term destination stewardship.

The Destination Facilities Director is accountable for ensuring that the destination operates to a clear 5-star standard, that service partners and internal teams deliver consistently against agreed expectations, and that Leasehold & Business Unit Property, Leasehold & Business Unit Property continues to strengthen its position as a high-quality live-work-play waterfront community. The role also safeguards its long-term physical, regulatory and environmental performance through proactive planning, governance and continuous improvement.

Responsibilities:

**Guest, Resident & Place Experience**

Accountable for a consistently 5-star destination experience across, Leasehold & Business Unit Property, ensuring residents, owners, tenants and guests experience a high-quality, well-presented and service-led environment at every touchpoint. Success is measured through presentation standards, resident and guest feedback, service recovery outcomes and the visible quality of the public realm, amenities, landscape, waterfront, retail and residential zones.

**Service Operations & FM Performance**

Accountable for reliable, seamless and hospitality-led service delivery across community management, facilities management, security, mobility, concierge and engineering interfaces. Ensures FM and service partners perform against agreed SLAs, escalations are resolved quickly, recurring service failures are addressed at root cause, and residents and tenants experience consistent service without operational friction.

**Commercial & Budget Outcomes**

Accountable for the effective management of Leasehold & Business Unit Property's master community budget, RERA service charge submission, reserve-fund adequacy, cost recovery and NOC-related revenue. Ensures the destination operates within approved budgets while maintaining the service quality, asset presentation and investment level required to protect long-term destination value.

**Service Culture & Team Effectiveness**

Accountable for building a service culture that shifts the destination operating model from reactive issue management to proactive, hospitality-led delivery. Ensures the Community Manager, wider community team and service partners work to clear standards, understand performance expectations, and are equipped to deliver consistent outcomes across experience, responsiveness, ownership and service recovery.

**Stakeholder, Government & Developer Confidence**

Accountable for strong stakeholder confidence in Leasehold & Business Unit Property's operating model by maintaining effective relationships with sub-developers, government authorities, strategic partners, residents, tenants, FM and hospitality service partners. Ensures forums, issues and competing priorities are managed with clarity, responsiveness and a consistent Shamal position.

**Placemaking & Destination Appeal**

Accountable for translating Leasehold & Business Unit Property's hospitality-led positioning into practical destination outcomes through a coordinated placemaking and activation calendar. Works with Shamal Marketing and Shamal Leisure & Entertainment to ensure the destination remains vibrant, engaging and commercially attractive without duplicating brand strategy ownership.

**Planning & Environmental Stewardship**

Accountable for protecting, Leasehold & Business Unit Property's long-term physical, regulatory and environmental performance as the destination matures. Ensures planning inputs, environmental assessment, conservation, waste management, cleaning, recycling, building approvals, signage, wayfinding, compliance processes and infrastructure renewal are managed in a coordinated way that supports sustainable destination value.

**Risk, Compliance & Crisis Readiness**

Accountable for ensuring Leasehold & Business Unit Property remains compliant, resilient and prepared for incidents, service failures and reputational risks. Oversees NOC management, key sustainability and safety certifications, escalation protocols and crisis response readiness, ensuring issues are managed quickly, visibly and with appropriate governance.

Qualifications:

* A hospitality qualification and RERA/Dubai real estate market familiarity are advantageous. Engineering degree would be desirable.
* Minimum 10 years' senior leadership as a General Manager or senior Director of Operations in a 5-star-or-above hotel, resort or branded residence – the non-negotiable qualifying experience for the role.
* Proven ownership of budget/P&L for a large asset (AED 25M+).
* Exposure to urban/master-plan governance, environmental compliance or development-approval processes is advantageous.

**For more information about Shamal, please visit our LinkedIn page:** https://www.linkedin.com/company/shamalholding/

Due to a high influx of profiles, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

**About us**
------------

The Institute of Making is a unique organisation that explores, celebrates, and investigates materials and processes through a wide range of activities. From large-scale public events to ground-breaking academic research projects, our diverse outputs and many audiences are united by a shared passion for materials and making. On a day-to-day basis, we bring together students and staff from across UCL, to provide a creative home in which to collaborate, innovate, contemplate and experience making from a wide range of disciplines. At the heart of the Institute of Making are our open-access facilities, which include multi-material workshops and the Materials Library.

The Institute of Making opened in Bloomsbury in 2013 with a workshop offering a broad range of tools and machinery for inducted members to use. The Materials Library is an ever-expanding repository of some of the most extraordinary materials on earth, including shape memory alloys and self-healing materials as well as some of the more ordinary materials that have also changed the world, like paper, beeswax, and copper. The Workshop and our Materials Library sit side-by-side, enabling users to experience first-hand the relationships between materials and tools that constitute processes of making. The space is also a stage for our expansive events programme and a home to a multitude of research projects.

The Institute of Making workshop team is responsible for establishing the safe and sustainable operation of the workshops and supporting our members in using the equipment and facilities across both the Bloomsbury and Stratford sites. The team’s main duties include supervising members’ access to the space, inducting new members, conducting tool trainings, advising members on design, materials, and processes, supporting the delivery of events, and contributing to the friendly, welcoming, imaginative, and open-minded atmosphere of the Institute of Making.

Our geography, which is comprised of about 1,800 square kilometers over nine different municipalities, is as beautiful, interesting and diverse as our people. Local government is organized in a two-tier structure and we work together with our local municipalities to provide residents and businesses access to a broad selection of services and resources.  
  
**WHAT WE OFFER**  
Recognized by Forbes as one of Canada’s Best Employers, we offer a collaborative, progressive workplace that takes pride in our organizational culture and is committed to living The 13+ Factors of Psychological Health and Safety in the Workplace – aligned with our vision to create strong, caring and safe communities both within and outside our walls.

* **Defined Benefit Pension Program** - With the Ontario Municipal Employees Retirement System (OMERS) defined benefit pension plan, you can confidently retire knowing that you will have income for life. Eligibility from date of hire as a full-time employee and includes employer-matched contributions.
* **Benefits and Wellness** - Employees and their loved ones have access to a comprehensive employer-paid benefits plan that includes extended health, dental and life insurance, access to a 24/7 Employee and Family Assistance Program and corporate discounts and purchase plans for day-to-day products and services.
* **Inclusive and Diverse Workforce** - We’re committed to fostering an environment that celebrates all dimensions of diversity and ensures everyone can develop to their full potential, participate freely in society and live with respect, dignity and freedom from discrimination. Our robust Inclusion, Diversity, Equity and Accessibility program continues to grow, and has been recognized by the United Nations and many other organizations for our leadership.

**ABOUT THE ROLE**

As a trusted advisor to the Commissioner, this position provides strategic leadership in advancing departmental and corporate priorities through the coordination of high-profile initiatives, organizational planning, and cross-functional collaboration. The role ensures the effective integration of corporate programs and strategic objectives, oversees change management initiatives supporting Integrated Services Plan priorities, and leads government relations and communications efforts.

The Manager provides expert advice and strategic briefing support to the Commissioner, CAO, and Chair’s Office, while contributing leadership and expertise in labour relations, collective bargaining strategies, organizational design, and restructuring initiatives that support the organization's long-term goals.

  

**WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING**

* Acts as a strategic advisor to the Commissioner.
* Responsible for department strategic planning initiatives including, providing leadership to development, implementation and monitoring of Human Services Plan, ensuring alignment with and support for Corporate Strategic Plan, Council priorities and Provincial directions in collaboration with Branches.
* Provides on-going leadership, overall coordination, change management planning and implementation, and integration of cyclical and ad-hoc departmental initiatives.
* Directs and oversees departmental initiatives to support stronger integration between human services programs and services in the department and with key external stakeholders.
* Takes key leadership role in the Department Emergency Operation Centre during emergencies as per Department Emergency and Business Continuity Plan; oversees Commissioner’s Office business continuity plan.
* Develops systems and processes to ensure the Commissioner is informed of strategic issues that require ongoing attention and/or planning.
* Provides key administration and implementation guidance for the Corporate culture and well-being initiatives to the Department, provides recommendation to the Commissioner in implementation and evolving of corporate strategy for the department by working within the Department Leadership Team (DLT).
* Partners and consults with the DLT to develop the leadership for department Diversity Equity and Inclusion Group; responsible to developing and managing implementation of strategy and goal setting process under the Corporate umbrella.
* Working under the corporate strategy, consults with Branch leaders to understand their leadership and management development needs to support succession planning and develops departmental strategies.
* Aligned with corporate direction, fosters building of strategic capabilities, skills, and learning mindsets required for the departmental needs.
* Provides leadership to strategic and long-term planning activities based on research/analysis of Regional initiatives, community needs, provincial initiatives and legislative requirements.
* Provides briefings to the Commissioner on current and anticipated issues and strategic opportunities, provides research and analysis on pertinent issues, develops policy or makes recommendations for appropriate action to the Commissioner.
* Develops and implements work plans for program policy and development strategies, ensuring strong linkages with other Departments, local municipalities, and other stakeholders.
Acts as the key liaison contact developing networks with Municipal, Provincial and Federal governments, business community, non-government agencies, charitable organizations, elected officials to exchange/provide information to maintain strong positive communication linkages promoting and supporting the Region's interests.  

**WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR**

* Successful completion of a University Degree in Business or Public Administration, Policy, Social Sciences, Humanities or a related field or approved equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Minimum seven (7) years demonstrated experience in a public sector environment with experience and responsibilities for policy/program initiatives and analysis, project management, change management strategies and research, and minimum of three (3) years of direct supervisory experience.
* Comprehensive knowledge of the relevant legislation and regulations with the ability to communicate the legislative significance and relevance to the work practices.
* Demonstrated political acumen, discernment, and ability to negotiate, mediate, facilitate and present information to a varied audience.
* Demonstrated experience and ability to lead or participate in cross-functional teams, foster cooperative and collaborative working relationships and to take multi partner projects to successful completion.
* Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to connect with a range of internal and external stakeholders while focusing on fostering collaborative work relationships.
* Strong policy and program development skills, including research techniques, advanced facilitation skills and demonstrated ability to build consensus across organizational lines.
* Demonstrated ability in the Region’s leadership core competencies.

Title: Senior Loyalty Manager
Description:
Job Description: The Senior Manager Loyalty – Programme Management & Operations is responsible for the end-to-end operational management, administration, execution, governance, and continuous improvement of the loyalty program. The role ensures that all operational capabilities, training, systems, processes, controls, and stakeholder functions work smoothly every day to deliver an excellent, reliable, scalable, and high-quality member experience.  
  
This position serves literally as a COO of the program, as the operational backbone of the loyalty program, driving excellence across platform operations, campaign execution support, member servicing, frontline enablement, governance, compliance, and issue resolution. The role is accountable for ensuring that loyalty propositions, benefits, campaigns, and customer experiences are launched flawlessly and operate effectively across all channels and touchpoints. The role is also responsible for developing relevant policies governing various operational aspects of the program to ensure that acceptable standards are adhered to and delivered consistently.

  

* Responsibilities: Loyalty Operations & Program Administration  
    
  Own day-to-day operational management of the loyalty program and develop  
    
  Establish, maintain, and continuously improve all loyalty operational processes  
    
  Develop and manage Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), process documentation, operational playbooks, and policies.  
    
  Ensure operational readiness across all loyalty channels and touchpoints.  
    
  Manage program administration activities including:  
    
  Tier management  
    
  Membership administration  
    
  Rewards administration  
    
  Benefit administration  
    
  Partner operational coordination  
    
  Drive operational efficiency through automation and process optimization initiatives.  
    
  Identify operational risks and implement preventive controls  
    
  Platform Operations, System Readiness & Configuration  
    
  Ensure loyalty platform stability, availability, and operational readiness  
    
  Manage routine platform configuration and operational updates  
    
  Coordinate with technology teams and vendors to maintain platform performance  
    
  Monitor system integrations between loyalty platforms, POS, Ecommerce, CRM, Customer Care, Payment Systems, and partner systems  
    
  Validate operational impacts of platform changes, releases, and enhancements  
    
  Maintain operational configuration governance and change management controls  
    
  Support platform roadmap execution from an operational perspective  
    
  Governance, Compliance & Controls  
    
  Establish and maintain loyalty governance frameworks.  
    
  Ensure compliance with internal policies, legal requirements, privacy regulations, and program rules.  
    
  Implement operational controls to protect the integrity of:  
    
  Membership data  
    
  Loyalty currencies  
    
  Rewards  
    
  Campaigns  
    
  Benefits  
    
  Conduct operational risk assessments and control reviews.  
    
  Support internal and external audits.  
    
  Develop fraud prevention and misuse detection controls along with Loss Prevention.  
    
  Incident Management & Operational Support  
    
  Lead operational incident management for loyalty-related issues.  
    
  Monitor loyalty operations for system, campaign, integration, or customer-impacting issues.  
    
  Coordinate issue investigation and resolution with:  
    
  IT teams  
    
  Vendors  
    
  CRM teams  
    
  Ecommerce teams  
    
  Retail operations  
    
  Establish incident severity classifications and escalation procedures.  
    
  Manage root-cause analysis and corrective action implementation.  
    
  Track operational incident KPIs and service recovery performance.  
    
  Quality Assurance & Testing  
    
  Own QA processes for all loyalty campaigns, benefits, and operational releases.  
    
  Conduct offer validation and end-to-end testing before deployment.  
    
  Coordinate User Acceptance Testing (UAT) across business stakeholders.  
    
  Develop and maintain testing methodologies and scenarios.  
    
  Ensure all defects are identified, documented, tracked, and resolved before launch.  
    
  Validate post-release performance and operational integrity.  
    
  Campaign Execution Support & Offer Operations  
    
  Lead operational setup and execution support for loyalty campaigns and promotions.  
    
  Ensure accurate configuration of:  
    
  Earn & Redemption campaigns  
    
  Bonus points campaigns  
    
  Tier accelerators  
    
  Partner promotions & Member-exclusive benefits  
    
  Coordinate campaign implementation across vendors, CRM teams, IT, Retail Operations, Ecommerce, and Marketing.  
    
  Validate campaign mechanics prior to launch.  
    
  Ensure campaign execution adheres to defined timelines and quality standards.  
    
  Frontline Enablement, Training & Knowledge Management (in collaboration with HR and Commercial)  
    
  Own loyalty training strategy for stores, customer care teams, and frontline colleagues.  
    
  Develop loyalty capability-building programs across the organization.  
    
  Create and maintain:  
    
  Training materials  
    
  E-learning modules  
    
  Playbooks  
    
  Quick reference guides  
    
  Operational manuals  
    
  Drive ongoing loyalty knowledge management initiatives.  
    
  Ensure frontline teams remain current on:  
    
  Program rules  
    
  Benefits  
    
  Campaigns  
    
  Member servicing procedures  
    
  Measure training effectiveness and knowledge adoption  
    
  Launch Readiness & Operational Deployment  
    
  Lead operational readiness assessments for launches.  
    
  Ensure all stakeholders are prepared prior to:  
    
  New campaigns  
    
  New rewards  
    
  New benefits  
    
  New partner integrations  
    
  New program features  
    
  Coordinate launch checklists and go-live reviews.  
    
  Validate readiness across systems, stores, customer care, and partner channels.  
    
  Manage post-launch monitoring and stabilization activities  
    
  Operational Audit & Compliance Monitoring  
    
  Conduct regular operational audits across channels.  
    
  Execute mystery shopping exercises to validate loyalty execution standards.  
    
  Assess compliance with operational procedures and loyalty policies.  
    
  Monitor consistency of loyalty delivery across stores and channels.  
    
  Identify improvement opportunities and execute corrective actions.  
    
  Member Care & Service Excellence  
    
  Own operational governance for loyalty-related customer service.  
    
  Establish member support standards and service processes.  
    
  Monitor member satisfaction and operational service performance.  
    
  Manage loyalty complaints, feedback, and escalations.  
    
  Define and monitor case management SLAs.  
    
  Ensure timely and accurate issue resolution.  
    
  Coordinate closely with Customer Care and Retail Operations teams to improve service quality  
    
  VIP Member Support & Escalation Management  
    
  Establish operational frameworks for VIP member servicing.  
    
  Manage complex and high-priority member cases.  
    
  Act as the escalation point for critical loyalty issues.  
    
  Coordinate rapid resolution of VIP member concerns.  
    
  Ensure service recovery protects customer loyalty and brand reputation  
    
  People Management Roles and Responsibilities  
    
  Excellent analytical and critical thinking skills, combined with strong verbal and written communication skills  
    
  Demonstrated ability to work effectively with cross-functional partners in a collaborative environment  
    
  Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders throughout the organization, both technical and non-technical

  

* Qualifications: Years of Experience  
    
  • 10+ years of experience in Loyalty Operations, CRM Operations, Customer Experience Operations  
    
  • Minimum 5 years managing complex multi-channel customer loyalty program operations.  
    
  • 3+ years of people management experience, including building and leading teams  
    
  • Experience operating loyalty technology platforms and integrations.  
    
  • Strong exposure to retail, luxury retail, omnichannel commerce, or customer engagement ecosystems  
    
  Knowledge and Skills  
    
  • Project management expertise and experience managing vendors and contractors  
    
  • Loyalty systems experience  
    
  • Operational excellence and business process design, management & improvement  
    
  • Loyalty Operations Management  
    
  • Project & Program Management  
    
  • Training & Change Management  
    
  • Incident & Service Management  
    
  • Governance & Controls  
    
  • UAT & Quality Assurance  
    
  • Customer Care Operations  
    
  • Vendor Management  
    
  • Data-driven problem solving.  
    
  • Experience in luxury retail and premium customer service environments.  
    
  • Lean Six Sigma, PMP, ITIL, or similar operational excellence certifications.
